paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Peter Rosh: Rashi explains that this was his name; Tosafot write that this was his father’s name. Rabbi Eliezer said: ‘When I went to Ardaskiya’—a place-name—‘I found Rabbi Yehoshua ben Peter Rosh sitting and discussing the law before Rabbi Meir. I said to him’—Rashi explains, to Rabbi Meir; Tosafot write that Rabbi Eliezer said it to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Peter Rosh—‘Are you acquainted with Rabbi Yehoshua bar Mammal?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’ He said—according to Rashi, Rabbi Meir; according to Tosafot, Rabbi Eliezer—‘Thus said Rabbi Yehoshua bar Mammal in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua’: Nazir 56b. In the Tosefta there, chapter 5: ‘Rabbi Eliezer said: When I went,’ and so forth. There in the Mishnah and Gemara, several times, and in Rashi and Tosafot, several times, ‘Rabbi Eliezer’ with a yod is a scribal error, and should read ‘Rabbi Elazar’; see his entry. He went to Ardaskiya, and so forth, and said: ‘Meir, are you acquainted?’ See there: he called him Meir because he was his colleague. In the Tosefta, Oholot, end of chapter 4, ‘Yehudah ben Petirosh’ appears three times; it is a scribal error and should read ‘Yehudah ben Peter Rosh,’ and so forth.
